stem:
The output potential difference (p.d.) of an alternating power supply is represented by

*V* = 320 sin(100π*t*)

where *V* is the p.d. in volts and *t* is the time in seconds.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Determine the root-mean-square (r.m.s.) p.d. of the power supply.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Determine the period *T* of the output.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.lead:
The power supply is connected to resistor R and a diode in the circuit shown in Fig. 10.1.

[[fig:f1]]
parts.text: State the name of the type of rectification produced by the diode in Fig. 10.1.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text:
On Fig. 10.2 sketch the variation with time *t* of the p.d. *V*₍R₎ across R from time *t* = 0 to time *t* = 40 ms.

[[fig:f2]]

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text: On Fig. 10.1, draw the symbol for a component that may be connected to produce smoothing of *V*₍R₎.

figures.caption: Fig. 10.1
figures.alt: A circuit with an alternating power supply, a diode in the top wire and resistor R in the right-hand wire.

figures.caption: Fig. 10.2
figures.alt: A square grid graph with vertical axis labelled V₍R₎ in volts from −400 to 400 and horizontal axis labelled t / ms from 0 to 40.
